title: John Rush's weekly roundup: YC vs 20k X followers, consistency, and copycat/scam risks
summary: A satirical weekly news digest from John Rush on tech, startups and indie hacking drama. Few durable lessons: audience on X can replace YC's moat, consistency wins on YouTube, and indie scene hazards like clones and presale scams. Links to his lazy SEO playbook tweet, but the playbook itself isn't in this text.

principles.text: A 20k X following gives a moat similar to a YC batch: founders reply to your DMs and VCs come inbound.
principles.quote: YC isn't "a must" anymore. Earning 20k followers on X brings a similar moat as being in YC batch cuz u can - DM successful founders and they answer - get huge inbound interest from VCs

principles.text: Winning on content is mostly about showing up consistently for a short, defined stretch.
principles.quote: What stops you from doing the same? What's your excuse? Just keep showing up for 2 months and u win.

principles.text: Successful products get cloned, even down to the name, so expect copycats as you gain traction.
principles.quote: a dude cloned my listingbott.com, even the name.

principles.text: Incumbents buy competitors and media to control distribution and narrative.
principles.quote: Semrush Acquires Third Door Media. Startups are playing real games now, buying news media to control the narrative

principles.text: Presale-and-disappear behavior burns buyers and hurts the whole maker ecosystem; trust is an asset.
principles.quote: A maker disappeared after the presale of his boilerplate.
